pulserver.pypulseq#

The drop-in replacement for pypulseq, and the single namespace for everything that produces a waveform, an event, or an acquisition plan. The complete upstream PyPulseq namespace is re-exported, then Pulserver’s Sequence and its extensions are layered on top, so one import covers both:

import pulserver.pypulseq as pp

seq = pp.Sequence()
excitation = pp.make_slice_selective_pulse(0.35, 5e-3, system=pp.Opts())
readout = pp.make_line_readout(pp.Opts(), (0.22, 0.22), (128, 128))

Sections below are organised by role, not by package layout; Pulserver extensions and their upstream counterparts appear side by side.

Sequence and system#

The sequence container and the scanner limits every factory is designed against. Pulserver’s Sequence subclasses upstream’s with a lower per-block overhead and support for custom labels and rotation/RF-shim extensions.

pulserver.pypulseq.Sequence

Sequence container tuned for append-only generation, with extensions.

pulserver.pypulseq.Opts

System limits of an MR scanner.

pulserver.pypulseq.SigpyPulseOpts

Filter and profile options for a SigPy-designed SLR pulse.

RF pulses — excitation and refocusing#

Slice-, slab-, frequency-selective and non-selective pulses. The Pulserver factories (make_hard_pulse and below) return a stateful Module carrying the RF event together with its selection and rephasing gradients, so a whole excitation is appended in one call and re-offset per slice. The upstream factories return bare events.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_hard_pulse

Create a non-selective rectangular (hard) pulse module.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_slr_pulse

Create an SLR-designed pulse, without requiring SigPy.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_sigpy_pulse

Create an SLR-designed pulse, without requiring SigPy.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_frequency_selective_pulse

Create a spectrally selective SLR pulse centred at freq_offset.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_slice_selective_pulse

Create a slice- or slab-selective excitation, gradients included.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_refocusing_pulse

Create a nominal 180-degree SLR refocusing pulse.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_inversion_pulse

Create a 180-degree inversion pulse, adiabatic by default.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_adiabatic_pulse

Create an adiabatic pulse module (B1-insensitive inversion/refocusing).

pulserver.pypulseq.make_block_pulse

Create a block (RECT or hard) pulse.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_sinc_pulse

Creates a radio-frequency sinc pulse event and optionally accompanying slice select and slice select rephasing trapezoidal gradient events.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_gauss_pulse

Create a [optionally slice selective] Gauss pulse.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_arbitrary_rf

Create an RF pulse with the given pulse shape.

RF pulses — multidimensional and spectral-spatial#

Pulses whose selectivity comes from playing RF concurrently with a gradient trajectory: small-tip 2D/3D excitation on a spiral or EPI path, and alternating-gradient spectral-spatial design.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_spsp_pulse

Create a spectral-spatial (SPSP) pulse on an alternating gradient.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_spatially_selective_pulse

Design a small-tip 2D/3D pulse on a gradient trajectory you supply.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_spiral_selective_pulse

Create a 2D selective pulse on an arbgrad-designed spiral.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_2d_selective_pulse

Create a 2D selective pulse, designing a spiral if none is supplied.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_3d_selective_pulse

Create a 3D selective pulse on a trajectory you supply.

Magnetization preparation#

Multi-block preparation modules — each bundles its pulses, inter-pulse delays and terminating spoiler into one appendable unit, with the scope labels that keep it out of the imaging FOV transform.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_fat_saturation_pulse

Create a fat-saturation module: spectral pulse plus 3-axis spoiler.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_mt_pulse

Create a magnetization-transfer saturation module.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_ihmt_pulse

Create an inhomogeneous-MT pulse train alternating +/- offset.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_t2prep_pulse

Create a T2 preparation module (90 - 180 - 90 with a terminating spoiler).

pulserver.pypulseq.make_t1t2_prep_pulse

Create hybrid T1/T2 preparation, storing the magnetization on -z.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_diffusion_prep

Create a diffusion preparation along z, at its full design b-value.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_bloch_siegert_pulse

Create a Bloch-Siegert B1-mapping pulse and its calibration constants.

Readout modules#

One factory per readout family. Each returns a stateful Module holding a whole shot — prewinders, echo train, ADCs, labels and rewinders — that is re-indexed per shot via set_state or by calling it. Dimensionality is inferred from matrix.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_line_readout

Create a Cartesian line readout: one phase-encode step per shot.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_epi_readout

Create an EPI readout: a whole echo train after one excitation.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_fse_readout

Create an FSE/TSE readout: a CPMG refocusing train, one line per echo.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_radial_readout

Create a 2D radial readout: one centre-crossing spoke per shot.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_spiral_readout

Create a 2D spiral readout: one interleaf per shot.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_rosette_readout

Create a 2D rosette readout: one petal per shot.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_noncartesian_3d_readout

Promote a natively 3D non-Cartesian gradient into a readout module.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_zte_readout

Create a ZTE readout: continuous gradient, excite-and-acquire per view.

Gradients#

Single gradient events and the algebra over them. make_crusher, make_spoiler, make_phase_encoding and make_phase_blip express the gradient in imaging terms — dephasing cycles, FOV, matrix — rather than area.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_trapezoid

Create a trapezoidal gradient event.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_arbitrary_grad

Creates a gradient event from an arbitrary waveform.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_extended_trapezoid

Create a gradient by specifying a set of points (amplitudes) at specified time points(times) at a given channel with given system limits.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_extended_trapezoid_area

Make the shortest possible extended trapezoid for given area and gradient start and end point.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_crusher

Build a single-axis crusher trapezoid.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_spoiler

Build a non-selective 3-axis crusher/spoiler gradient set.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_phase_encoding

Build the phase-encode template trapezoid and per-view area array.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_phase_blip

Create a phase blip spanning steps Cartesian k-space cells.

pulserver.pypulseq.add_gradients

Returns the superposition of several gradients.

pulserver.pypulseq.scale_grad

Scales the gradient with the scalar.

pulserver.pypulseq.split_gradient

Splits a trapezoidal gradient into slew up, flat top and slew down.

pulserver.pypulseq.split_gradient_at

Splits a trapezoidal gradient into two extended trapezoids defined by the cut line.

pulserver.pypulseq.points_to_waveform

1D interpolate amplitude values amplitudes at time indices times as per the gradient raster time grad_raster_time to generate a gradient waveform.

pulserver.pypulseq.traj2grad

Design a hardware-feasible gradient from a k-space path you specify.

Arbitrary-gradient design#

pulserver.pypulseq.arbgrad designs slew- and amplitude-limited base waveforms for non-Cartesian trajectories (spiral, rosette, arbitrary k-space paths) with a vendored MRArbGrad C++ core, and reports how many shots cover k-space. Shot ordering and rotation stay in Python.

pulserver.pypulseq.arbgrad

Arbitrary-gradient waveform design for non-Cartesian trajectories.

ADC and timing#

ADC event creation, raster-feasible readout timing, and the duration/centre queries used to solve TE and TR budgets.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_adc

Create an ADC readout event.

pulserver.pypulseq.calc_adc_timing

Return an ADC dwell and readout duration legal on both time rasters.

pulserver.pypulseq.calc_adc_segments

Calculate splitting of the ADC in segments with equal samples.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_delay

Creates a delay event.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_soft_delay

Create a soft delay extension event for dynamic timing adjustment.

pulserver.pypulseq.calc_duration

Calculate the duration of an event or block.

pulserver.pypulseq.calc_rf_center

Calculate the time point of the effective rotation calculated as the peak of the radio-frequency amplitude for the shaped pulses and the center of the pulse for the block pulses.

pulserver.pypulseq.calc_rf_bandwidth

Calculate the spectrum of the RF pulse.

pulserver.pypulseq.calc_ramp

Join the points k0 and k_end in three-dimensional k-space in minimal time, observing the gradient and slew limits (max_grad and max_slew respectively), and the gradient strength G0 before k0[:, 1] and Gend after k_end[:, 1].

pulserver.pypulseq.align

Sets delays of the objects within the block to achieve the desired alignment of the objects in the block.

Timing is validated with Sequence.check_timing().

Sampling patterns#

Which k-space locations are acquired, and in which order — kept numeric and sequence-independent. A SamplingPattern pairs the sampled support with per-shot index arrays; readout modules consume its coordinates. See the sampling reference for the full model.

pulserver.pypulseq.SamplingPattern

Sampled support plus its shot-by-shot acquisition order.

Cartesian masks and echo-train ordering#

Undersampling masks with a calibration region, and the orderings that split a (ky, kz) point set into FSE echo trains or MPRAGE segments.

pulserver.pypulseq.sampled_lines

Return the sampled view indices for uniform undersampling + ACS block.

pulserver.pypulseq.random_mask

Generate a uniform-random undersampling mask with a calibration region.

pulserver.pypulseq.caipirinha_mask

Generate a 2D CAIPIRINHA lattice undersampling mask.

pulserver.pypulseq.poisson_disc_mask

Generate a variable-density Poisson-disc undersampling mask.

pulserver.pypulseq.from_mask

Turn a Cartesian mask into ordered shots of absolute (ky, kz) indices.

pulserver.pypulseq.fse_linear_order

Linear (raster) echo-train ordering over a (ky, kz) point set.

pulserver.pypulseq.fse_radial_order

Center-out radial (wedge) echo-train ordering.

pulserver.pypulseq.fse_radial_adaptive_order

Adaptive radial echo-train ordering (individually parameterized trains).

pulserver.pypulseq.fse_shuffling_order

Randomly shuffled echo-train ordering (T2 Shuffling).

EPI and relative-shift trains#

Plans expressed as a per-shot start plus a list of blip increments — the natural form for EPI, segmented blipped-CAIPI, and EPTI-like schedules.

pulserver.pypulseq.from_relative_shifts

Build a sampling plan from per-shot start points and blip increments.

pulserver.pypulseq.skipped_caipi

Build a segmented skipped-CAIPI 3D-EPI sampling plan.

Non-Cartesian tilts#

Spoke and interleaf directions for radial and 3D centre-out acquisitions, and their conversion to rotation matrices for a rotated base waveform.

pulserver.pypulseq.radial_2d

Generate 2D radial spoke angles and their acquisition segments.

pulserver.pypulseq.golden_angles

Return n full-circle golden-angle spoke angles, in radians.

pulserver.pypulseq.uniform_angles

Return n equally spaced full-circle spoke angles, in radians.

pulserver.pypulseq.golden_means_3d

Generate 3D centre-out spoke directions from the 2D golden means.

pulserver.pypulseq.spiral_phyllotaxis

Generate 3D spoke directions on a spiral phyllotaxis, interleaved.

pulserver.pypulseq.directions_to_rotations

Convert spoke directions into minimal-angle rotation matrices.

Slice order and outer loops#

Slice/SMS grouping with per-band frequency offsets, and the generic helpers for enumerating the loops outside the readout.

pulserver.pypulseq.slice_groups

Plan the slice loop: acquisition order, SMS banding, and positions.

pulserver.pypulseq.SliceGroup

One excitation's worth of slices, with their physical positions.

pulserver.pypulseq.outer_product

Enumerate every combination of the named outer loop dimensions.

pulserver.pypulseq.outer_inner_order

Pair every outer index with the full inner range, as one shot each.

pulserver.pypulseq.linear_order

Split n sequential views into echo trains of length etl.

pulserver.pypulseq.chunk_indices

Split a flat index list into consecutive chunks of at most size.

RF phase and flip-angle schedules#

Per-repetition phase and flip-angle lists: quadratic RF spoiling, arbitrary phase cycling, and Alsop-style variable refocusing trains.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_rf_spoiling_schedule

Return the quadratic RF-spoiling phase schedule, in radians.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_phase_cycling_schedule

Tile a fixed phase cycle to length entries, in radians.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_traps_schedule

Return a TRAPS variable refocusing flip-angle schedule, in radians.

Labels, rotations, and extensions#

Per-block metadata: counter labels consumed by the reconstruction, block rotations, RF shim vectors, and hardware triggers. Pulserver’s make_label accepts user-defined label strings in addition to the built-in set.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_label

Create a label event without validating label against the built-in list.

pulserver.pypulseq.get_supported_labels

Return the built-in Pulseq label names, in file order.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_rotation

Create a rotation extension event.

pulserver.pypulseq.rotate

Rotates the corresponding gradient(s) about the given axis by the specified amount.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_rf_shim

Create an RF shim extension event.

pulserver.pypulseq.make_trigger

Create a trigger halt event for a synchronization with an external signal from a given channel with an optional

pulserver.pypulseq.make_digital_output_pulse

Create a digital output pulse event a.k.a.

Shapes and utilities#

Pulseq shape compression, unit conversion, and tracing helpers. Upstream binds compress_shape, decompress_shape and convert to their modules rather than to the functions, so pp.compress_shape is a module; the callables are documented below at their canonical location and are reached as pp.compress_shape.compress_shape.

pypulseq.compress_shape.compress_shape

Compress a gradient or pulse shape waveform using a run-length compression scheme on the derivative.

pypulseq.decompress_shape.decompress_shape

Decompress a gradient or pulse shape compressed with a run-length compression scheme on the derivative.

pypulseq.convert.convert

Converts gradient amplitude or slew rate from unit from_unit to unit to_unit with gyromagnetic ratio gamma.

pulserver.pypulseq.round_half_up

Avoid banker's rounding inconsistencies; from https://realpython.com/python-rounding/#rounding-half-up

pulserver.pypulseq.enable_trace

Enable tracing where sequence events and blocks were created.

pulserver.pypulseq.disable_trace

Disabling tracing where sequence events and blocks were created.
